frontier.hypothesis: A 68-instruction spelling exists that makes the biased command loop-carried WITHOUT adding in-loop references to it - which would reproduce probe H's measured 8x demotion of pseudo 75 (pri 75000 -> 9333, below the walker) on a legal shape.
frontier.mechanism: H's demotion comes from two things at once: the latch definition lengthens 75's live range (4 -> 15) and removes in-loop uses (nrefs 10 -> 7). It costs one preheader instruction. Probe L paid that instruction with head tests on cmd and gave the references straight back. The payment must therefore come from somewhere that does not touch cmd: the preheader (11 pad stores + the ptr load + the guard test), pseudo 72 (pad), or the operand-byte path. Probe K shows the u8->u32 promotion on c is worth -3 insns, so a partial widening (one narrowed use, not all three) may be worth exactly -1.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate -1-instruction edits that leave cmd's reference set alone and pair each with the H tail: (a) narrow/widen exactly one of c's three uses (the loop test, the 0xFF test, the <0x80 test) to shed one andi/zero-extend without disturbing the head-test operands; (b) fold the preheader guard `if (c != 0)` into the first tail read by rotating the loop; (c) express one preheader pad store through the walker's base register. Measure each with sandbox for build_insns FIRST (the gate is 68), and only extract.py the ones that land on 68.

frontier.hypothesis: The operand byte val (pseudo 76) can be demoted below the walker only by breaking its 12-way death pattern, and the aggregate-store shape that would do so is the one axis of the switch that no session has measured.
frontier.mechanism: 76 needs livelen >= 68 (pri < 15483) and staging caps it at 31, because it dies once per switch arm and reg_live_length only accumulates the blocks in which it is live. If the twelve arm stores were replaced by one store through a dispatch-selected destination, val would die once and its live range would span the whole dispatch. That changes the switch shape, so it is only worth measuring if the insn count can hold at 68.
frontier.next_probe: Measure the two shapes that keep a jump table but a single store: (a) each arm assigns only a destination offset and a single `pad[off] = val;` follows the switch; (b) each arm assigns a `u8 *dst` and a single `*dst = val;` follows. Check build_insns before anything else - the target's twelve separate sb instructions make 68 unlikely, and a fast negative here permanently closes the 76 leg of the s18 relief curve.

frontier.hypothesis: The s18 336-order constraint set (pri(73) > pri(76) > {pri(75), pri(85)}) is specific to the eight-allocno base configuration and does NOT describe what probes H and L need, because both drop allocno 85 entirely.
frontier.mechanism: s18 enumerated 8! orders over the base allocno set. H has 8 allocnos with a different membership (85 gone, 86 promoted to a 6-reference holder); L has 7. The reachable-order analysis, and therefore the relief curve, has never been recomputed for either configuration - so the real requirement for the staged family is unknown, and H may be much closer to (or further from) a target-reaching order than the base-set curve suggests.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the s18 pipeline (order_closure.py then order_constraints.py then relief_curve.py) against s19/model_H_cmd_staged.json and s19/model_L_staged_tests_on_cmd.json, using goal_from_tgt to re-derive the target disposition for each allocno set. Report the new necessary precedences and the new relief curve BEFORE spelling any more C - if the staged configuration needs less than the base one, the 68-insn payment above is the whole remaining problem.
